sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for logging
sections.what: Brings in Python's built-in logging tools, a helper that rotates log files, and the shared config.
sections.why: Python already has logging built in, and the level and file settings come from the config.
sections.watch_out: The config must load successfully first, because this module reads settings as soon as it loads.

sections.name: setup_logger
sections.title: Building the app's log writer
sections.what: Creates a logger that prints messages to the screen and also writes them to a log file, which is replaced with a fresh one when it gets large. By default it keeps 5 old copies at about 10 MB each.
sections.why: Gives a written record of what the app did, which helps when something fails, especially in unattended scheduled runs.
sections.watch_out: An invalid log level name in the config crashes the program at startup, and later config changes are ignored once the logger is set up.

summary: Sets up one shared logger that writes messages to the screen and to a rotating log file.
purpose: Gives every module one consistent place to record progress and errors.
why: Likely reason: a saved log is needed to debug runs that happen without someone watching, such as the scheduled pipeline.
how: 1) Get or create a named logger. 2) Stop early if handlers already exist. 3) Read the level, message format, and file path from config. 4) Add a console handler. 5) Create the log folder if needed. 6) Add a rotating file handler. 7) Create the default logger when the module loads.
inputs: Settings for log level, message format, log file path, maximum file size, and number of backup files, plus an optional logger name.
outputs: A logger object, console messages, and a log file in the logs folder by default.
risks: A bad log level name stops every module that imports this one. Log files can contain error text from failed requests, so they may hold sensitive detail.
debug: If no log file appears, check the logging file setting and folder permissions. If messages are too few or too many, check the logging level in config and the LOG_LEVEL environment variable. If startup fails with an attribute error, the level name is probably wrong.
